title: WILL o GOING TO
subtitle: Will, going to and present continuous · el futuro

map.center: El inglés tiene 3 futuros: will (decido ahora), going to (ya lo planeé) y present continuous (cita fija).

explain.es: En español casi siempre decimos «voy a…» o usamos el futuro (iré, llamaré). En inglés hay tres formas principales y la elección depende de cuándo tomaste la decisión y de cuánto de seguro es el plan: will para decisiones del momento, promesas, ofrecimientos y opiniones; going to para planes ya decididos y predicciones con pruebas; y el present continuous para citas y planes fijos con día y hora.
explain.en: English has three main future forms: will (instant decisions, promises, offers, opinions), going to (plans, predictions with evidence) and the present continuous (fixed arrangements).
formula: Sujeto + *am / is / are going to* + infinitivo

explain.title: 1 · WILL: forma
explain.es: will es igual para todas las personas (¡sin -s!) y va seguido del infinitivo sin to. En la conversación se contrae: I'll, you'll, she'll. La negativa es won't (= will not). En la pregunta, Will va delante del sujeto.
explain.en: will + infinitive without to, the same for all persons. Negative: won't. Question: Will + subject + verb?

examples.en: I'll send you the photos later.
Will you be at home tonight? — Yes, I will.

items.es: ¿Lo decides ahora, te ofreces, prometes o pides algo? → will.
¿Es un plan que ya tenías decidido? → going to.
¿Ves pruebas de que va a pasar? → going to.
¿Es una cita organizada con día y hora? → present continuous.
Revisa la forma: will + infinitivo · am/is/are going to + infinitivo · am/is/are + -ing.

explain.title: 2 · WILL: decisiones al momento y ofrecimientos
explain.es: Usamos will cuando decidimos algo en ese mismo momento, sin haberlo pensado antes, y para ofrecernos a hacer algo. Muy típico en restaurantes y tiendas: I'll have the chicken (= tomaré / me pido el pollo). Para ofrecerte en forma de pregunta usamos Shall I…?
explain.en: will for decisions made at the moment of speaking and offers. Offer questions: Shall I…?

examples.en: What would you like? — I'll have the fish, please.
examples.es: ¿Qué va a tomar? — Pescado, por favor.

examples.en: Those bags look heavy. I'll carry one for you.
examples.es: Esas bolsas parecen pesadas. Te llevo una.

examples.en: It's dark in here. Shall I turn on the light?

explain.title: Truco de la agenda
explain.es: Piensa en tu agenda 📒. ¿Está escrito con día y hora? → present continuous. ¿Está en tu cabeza (lo has decidido)? → going to. ¿Se te ocurre ahora mismo? → will. Y si «voy a» es una decisión del momento (¡Voy yo!), en inglés es I'll go!
explain.en: In the diary → present continuous. In your head → going to. Just decided → will.

explain.title: 3 · WILL: promesas, peticiones y predicciones sin pruebas
explain.es: will también sirve para prometer (I'll always love you), pedir algo (Will you help me?) y hacer predicciones basadas en nuestra opinión, no en pruebas. Por eso suele ir con I think, I hope, I'm sure, probably, maybe. Ojo: I don't think…will, no I think…won't.
explain.en: will for promises, requests and predictions based on opinion: I think…, I'm sure…, probably.

examples.es: Te prometo que no se lo diré a nadie.

examples.en: I think Spain will win the World Cup.
examples.es: Creo que España ganará el Mundial.

examples.en: I don't think it will be expensive.

explain.title: 4 · GOING TO: planes e intenciones
explain.es: be going to + infinitivo expresa un plan o intención decidido antes de hablar. Es el «voy a…» del español. El verbo be cambia según el sujeto (am / is / are). Con el verbo go, en vez de I'm going to go to Paris solemos decir I'm going to Paris.
explain.en: be going to + infinitive for plans and intentions decided before speaking.
formula: Sujeto + *am / is / are going to* + infinitivo
Sujeto + *'m not / isn't / aren't going to* + infinitivo

examples.en: I'm going to start a Master's in September.
examples.es: Voy a empezar un máster en septiembre.

examples.en: We're not going to buy a car this year.
examples.es: No vamos a comprar coche este año.

examples.en: Are you going to watch the final? — Of course I am!

explain.title: 5 · GOING TO: predicciones con pruebas
explain.es: Usamos going to para predecir algo cuando vemos pruebas ahora de que va a pasar: nubes negras, un vaso al borde de la mesa, un marcador 4-0 a falta de 2 minutos. Compara: I think it'll rain tomorrow (opinión) / Look at those clouds! It's going to rain (lo estoy viendo).
explain.en: going to for predictions based on what we can see now.
formula: Prueba ahora → sujeto + *is / are going to* + infinitivo

examples.en: Look at those black clouds! It's going to rain.
examples.es: ¡Mira esas nubes negras! Va a llover.

examples.en: Careful! That glass is going to fall.
examples.es: ¡Cuidado! Ese vaso se va a caer.

examples.en: They're 4-0 up. They're going to win.

explain.title: 6 · PRESENT CONTINUOUS: citas y planes fijos
explain.es: Para planes ya organizados con otras personas, con día, hora o lugar (está en la agenda, has reservado, has quedado), usamos el present continuous con una expresión de futuro. En español también usamos el presente: «Mañana ceno con Ana» = I'm having dinner with Ana tomorrow.
explain.en: Present continuous + future time for fixed arrangements (in the diary, booked, agreed with others).
formula: Sujeto + *am / is / are* + *verbo-ing* + tonight / on Friday / at 6

examples.en: I'm meeting Laura for coffee at five.
examples.es: He quedado con Laura a las cinco para tomar café.

examples.en: We're flying to Dublin on Saturday morning.
examples.es: Volamos a Dublín el sábado por la mañana.

explain.title: WILL o GOING TO: ¿cuándo lo decidiste?
explain.title_en: will or going to: when did you decide?
explain.es: La diferencia clave está en el momento de la decisión. Si lo decides mientras hablas → will. Si ya lo habías decidido antes → going to.

cols.head: ⚡ will · lo decido ahora
items: We've got no milk! — Oh, I'll buy some.
The phone's ringing. — I'll get it!

cols.head: 🗓️ going to · ya lo decidí
items: I'm going to buy milk. Do you need anything?
I'm going to call Mum after dinner.

explain.title: Predicciones: opinión o pruebas
explain.es: Las dos sirven para predecir, pero will se basa en lo que pienso y going to en lo que veo.
explain.en: will = what I think. going to = what I can see.

cols.head: 💭 will · lo creo
items: I think it'll be sunny tomorrow.
You'll love Lisbon, I'm sure.

cols.head: 👀 going to · lo veo
items: Look at the sky. It's going to be sunny.
She's packing. She's going to leave.

explain.title: GOING TO o PRESENT CONTINUOUS
explain.es: A menudo las dos son posibles. going to = intención (lo quiero hacer). present continuous = algo ya organizado (reservado, acordado, con hora).
explain.en: going to = intention. present continuous = arranged (booked, agreed, with a time).

items: I'm going to visit Japan one day.

cols.head: 📌 present cont. · ya organizado

exercises.title: ¿Verdadero o falso?

items.q: We use «will» for decisions we make at the moment of speaking.
«She wills come» is correct.
items.why: will no lleva -s: She will come.

items.q: «Look at the clouds! It's going to rain» is a prediction with evidence.
We use the present continuous for fixed arrangements with a time.
«I will to go» is correct.
items.why: will + infinitivo sin to: I will go.

items.q: «I think it won't rain» is the most natural way to say it.
items.why: Más natural: I don't think it will rain.

items.q: «Shall I open the window?» is an offer.
«I'm going to study Medicine» is a decision made at the moment of speaking.

exercises.title: Lee y contesta
exercises.es: Lee los mensajes de Hugo. Marca T (true) o F (false) y contesta las preguntas.

text: To Mum: Hi Mum! Just to let you know my plans for the summer. I'm going to work in a café in Bristol for two months to improve my English. I'm flying there on 1st July — I booked the ticket yesterday!
To Lena: Hey Lena! Are you free tonight? I'm meeting Jorge and Ana at the new burger place at 9. Come with us! And don't worry about your bike, I'll fix it tomorrow, I promise.
To Jorge: Mate, have you seen those black clouds? It's going to rain any minute! Shall I bring an umbrella for you? Also, I think Ana will be late, as usual 😂. I'll wait for you both at the entrance.

items.q: Hugo is going to work in a café in Bristol.
Hugo hasn't bought his plane ticket yet.
Hugo is meeting his friends at 9 tonight.
When is Hugo flying to Bristol?
What does Hugo promise Lena?

items.q: Why does Hugo think it's going to rain?
items.a: Because he can see black clouds (there's evidence).

items.q: What does Hugo offer Jorge?

checklist.es: Uso will para decisiones del momento, ofrecimientos, promesas y peticiones.
checklist.en: I use will for instant decisions, offers, promises and requests.

checklist.es: Uso will con I think / I'm sure para predicciones basadas en mi opinión.
checklist.en: I use will for predictions based on opinion.

checklist.es: Uso going to para planes ya decididos y predicciones con pruebas.
checklist.en: I use going to for plans and predictions with evidence.

checklist.es: Uso el present continuous para citas con día y hora.
checklist.en: I use the present continuous for arrangements.

checklist.es: Escribo will + infinitivo sin to y sin -s; la negativa es won't.
checklist.en: I write will + verb (no to, no -s). Negative: won't.

checklist.es: Ofrezco ayuda con Shall I…? y digo I don't think… will.
checklist.en: I can offer with Shall I…? and say I don't think… will.
